verdicts.note: Appointed September 2021 and elected to a full term in 2022, 3,214 to 2,884 (S1, S6, S9); his pamphlet statement runs on his record ('When you elected me four years ago... I get results') (S1), plus prior hospital and library board service (S1, S6). An incumbent explicitly campaigning on results is the pole_a case; -2/high stands and all three citations are in his dossier and support it.

S4 quotes 'maintaining essential services while holding taxes down' and 'accountable to taxpayers'. That is a hold-the-line stance with no tax-cut proposal and no recorded levy vote, so -1 (not -2) at medium is right. S3 is weak support (the dossier cites it for road levy shifts and road, snowplow and public-safety priorities, which are budget-allocation points, not taxes), but S4 alone carries the score. Nothing in either dossier points toward pole_b.

S4: county government should 'spend carefully' and 'remain accountable to taxpayers'; S1: he opposed road levy shifts as 'a short-term fix'. Tried to refute: he also touts securing more road and snowplow money and nearly $5 million for Kaniksu Village housing (S1, S6), which is investment rather than restraint, and the road levy stance protects a dedicated fund rather than cutting. That mixed record caps it at magnitude 1 and medium, but his stated philosophy is restraint-first, so -1/medium stands.

First run for county office against an incumbent elected in 2022, with small-business and volunteer-board experience only (S1, S4). Tried to refute: she does not run as an outsider or on generational change, and is endorsed by local mayors, Commissioner Gentle and the auditor (S5), an establishment profile. But the axis measures the record-versus-new profile, and per precedent (Cowlitz D3, Clark clerk) first-time candidates running on credentials rather than on newness score +1, not +2. The basis already says 'rather than an outsider overhaul'. +1/medium stands; S1 and S3 are in her dossier and support the first-run and collaborative-leadership points.
